A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same numerical-reproducibility study and LayerCast method. All pages, including appendices, are readable; retained equations, figures, tables, and sections can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments measuring inference accuracy, output divergence, and numerical variability across precision and hardware settings, together with LayerCast evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds results for Qwen3-32B, GPQA Diamond, HuggingFace Transformers, and LayerCast on another model.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same LayerCast procedure: load in FP32, store linear weights and biases in BF16, and upcast them individually for FP32 computation. The new discussion of batch-invariant kernels does not incorporate them into LayerCast.

E1.justification: V2 adds GPQA Diamond evaluation using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, extending coverage from mathematics and code generation into graduate-level science reasoning (Appendix C.1, Table 11). The original five benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: The precision comparisons and LayerCast's BF16/FP32 comparators remain unchanged. Qwen3-32B is an additional model under study, and Transformers supplies a backend verification experiment. Batch-invariant kernels are discussed but not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: V2 substantially extends experimental settings through Qwen3-32B tests, separate Transformers-backend verification, and LayerCast evaluation on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B across A100 and L40S GPUs. Existing protocols remain intact. The new Qwen3-32B experiment has 12 BF16 configurations but only nine feasible FP32 configurations because two-L40S settings run out of memory.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a targeted verification of whether instability depends on vLLM/PagedAttention, testing two models on AIME’24 with standard Transformers. The original GPU-count, batch-size, and GPU-type ablations are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions use 16 and 64 sampling runs for AIME’24 and four for MATH500, with the same standard-deviation reporting across runtime configurations. New experiments extend this reporting practice without introducing new seed protocols, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing table values are retained, while four new result sets broaden the empirical evidence. Qwen3-32B has reported accuracy standard deviations of 5.02% for BF16 and 1.11% for FP32 over 12 and nine configurations respectively; GPQA Diamond reports 3.03% and 1.96%. Table 12 adds Transformers results, and Table 26 reports constant 36.67% accuracy for LayerCast and FP32 on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B. These are additional results, not improvements over matched v1 experiments.

T1.justification: The floating-point examples, reduction formulation, and metric definitions remain substantively unchanged. Appendix F's new discussion of deterministic upcasting is qualitative reasoning, without a new formal assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about precision-dependent reproducibility, FP32's greater stability, and LayerCast's memory/stability tradeoff. The new title and supporting experiments do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving GPU-kernel choices, the scope of batch-invariant operations, deterministic upcasting, and generality across models and backends. It removes v1's explicit limitations concerning models above 70B, other accelerators, architectures and modalities, along with the broader-impact discussion of additional computational costs.

D1.justification: For the added experiments, v2 specifies standard Transformers without vLLM/PagedAttention and documents the FP32 memory constraint for Qwen3-32B on two L40S GPUs. Existing prompt templates, the LayerCast implementation description, and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds references to He/Thinking Machines Lab's batch-invariant inference work, NVIDIA CUTLASS documentation, and Orca. It positions batch invariance as addressing batching changes rather than GPU-type or tensor-parallel-size changes. The existing related-work survey is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, conference footer, and Section 2 headings, makes localized wording corrections, and expands selected explanations. The appendices are reorganized, with random sampling preceding LayerCast and new verification subsections added; most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 10–12 and 26, relocates and renumbers existing tables, and adjusts figure placement and spacing. All nine figures retain their substantive content, and the established visual style and table formats are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The larger-model, science-domain, alternative-backend, and second-model LayerCast evaluations strengthen evidence beyond v1's original experimental scope, particularly by checking dependence on vLLM. These are useful extensions of unchanged findings. Their benefit is tempered by removal of still-relevant limitations about models above 70B, other accelerators, and other architectures or modalities. Overall, v2 provides a modest net improvement in empirical support.
